site.name: runeforge-docs
site.summary: runeforge-docs Fictional state-management JavaScript library "Runeforge" official documentation site (Redux / Zustand-style ergonomics). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Sticky topbar with brand+version pill, doc tabs, ⌘K search trigger, version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars; **three-column layout**: left categorized TOC tree (5 sections, 26 items), center page with hero / install code-tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) / "Hello, store" code-tabs (5 framework adapters: Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3) with copy button / 3-tile "three things to remember" / 6-row why-table comparing to Redux / Zustand / Jotai / next-steps list / prev/next pager; right-side on-this-page TOC. - `guide-quickstart.html` — 5-minute tutorial. Step-by-step build of a counter store, todo list with derived store, async fetcher with `asyncSlice()`, and devtools install. Lots of code blocks and an info / success callout. - `guide-stores.html` — Stores reference. Store API table; reading + subscribing; immutability warning callout; composing with `derive()`; slicing with `store.select()`; SSR (`toJSON` / `fromJSON`); testing pattern. - `guide-actions.html` — Actions & selectors. Action rules; selector c

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full runeforge-docs system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The docs site has strong orientation and scannability overall: onboarding, reference anchors, and examples filtering all generally work, and search opens a recognizable command palette. The biggest UX risks are mobile touch usability and clarity of state changes: the header contains many undersized controls, the version selector is unlabeled and appears inert, and the examples filter/reset flow does not give trustworthy feedback on mobile. Coverage is broad across the main pages, but several top-nav destinations and some reference sections remain untested, so the issues below focus on the consistently observed interaction problems.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the Runeforge docs site as a documentation/product UX, with emphasis on the primary getting-started path and the adjacent reference/example paths that a new user would use to evaluate and adopt the library.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the docs home page and validate the main onboarding path: introduction, install instructions, hello-store examples, and navigation to the quickstart. Then cover the core concept pages and the API reference to confirm the docs hierarchy, in-page navigation, and content depth are coherent. Finish by checking examples and key mobile behaviors, with special attention to controls that are already flagged as small or unlabeled in the prescan.
assumptions: The main exploration flow is documentation-led rather than a transactional checkout flow, so success means clear discoverability, navigation, and comprehension across docs pages.

The visible top-level links are the authoritative site map for the run; items shown as '#' may be placeholders or non-functional and should be treated as lower-confidence adjacency, not guaranteed destinations.
The site should remain usable without console/network errors; the main validation focus is content structure, control behavior, and responsive ergonomics.
Search, version switching, theme toggle, and copy buttons are expected to be interactive even though only some are explicitly shown in the prescan.
risk_hotspots: Top-bar controls on index.html: Search docs ⌘K, version select, theme toggle, and GitHub/star link are small tap targets on mobile and include an unlabeled select in the prescan.
Left navigation / docs tree on index.html: several entries are placeholder '#' links, so verify which items navigate and whether the active state is clear.
Code-tab switches and copy buttons on index.html, guide-quickstart.html, and examples.html: important for reading/install flows and likely to be error-prone on mobile.
guide-quickstart.html: dense step-by-step tutorial with multiple code blocks and callouts; verify that progression through install/counter/todo/async/devtools remains readable and scannable.
guide-stores.html and guide-actions.html: concept-heavy pages with tables and code examples; confirm anchors, headings, and explanatory structure are easy to traverse.

findings.user_goal: Switch documentation versions from the header
findings.problem: The version selector is hard to understand and does not give visible confirmation when activated, so users cannot tell whether a version change is available or happened.
findings.evidence: On index.html and api-reference.html, clicking the version select produced no visible menu, state change, or URL change. It is also flagged as a missing input label / unlabeled select in the DOM summary and layout warnings.
findings.why_it_matters: Version switching is a core docs task. If the control looks inert and lacks a label, users may miss important version-specific docs or assume the feature is broken.
findings.suggestion: Give the control a visible label or stronger affordance, and show an obvious open state or version-change confirmation when tapped/clicked.
findings.source_hint: index.html / api-reference.html top bar, select v3.4 (latest)

findings.user_goal: Use the docs header on a phone without fighting the layout
findings.problem: The top bar contains many tap targets that are below mobile size guidance, making primary navigation and utilities difficult to use on touch screens.
findings.evidence: Across index.html, api-reference.html, and examples.html mobile/desktop checks, controls like Docs, API, Blog, Community, Search docs ⌘K, theme toggle, star button, and the brand link were repeatedly flagged as under 44px tall; the mobile observation also shows horizontal overflow.
findings.why_it_matters: When common actions are cramped or too small, mobile users are more likely to mis-tap or avoid the header altogether, which slows navigation and increases frustration.
findings.suggestion: Increase hit areas to at least 44px high, reduce header density on mobile, and consider collapsing secondary links into a menu.
findings.source_hint: Global header on index.html / examples.html / api-reference.html

findings.user_goal: Clear the examples filter and return to the full gallery
findings.problem: The clear/reset affordance in the mobile examples filter is visible but does not provide reliable feedback that the filter was cleared.
findings.evidence: On examples.html mobile, repeated clicks on the filter input/clear area left the query text as `async` and the gallery remained filtered; the final observation still shows the narrowed set rather than a reset state. The recent trajectory also notes no obvious text or URL change after the action.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot trust the clear action, they may think the gallery is stuck or broken, which is especially painful when trying to recover from a narrow search on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Make the clear action explicit and deterministic: ensure the x control clears the field, immediately restores the full card set, and shows a brief visible reset state.

findings.user_goal: Browse and filter example cards on a phone
findings.problem: The examples page overflows horizontally on mobile, so the filter controls and card grid sit in a wider-than-screen layout that can require extra panning.
findings.evidence: The mobile observation reports page width 536px versus a 390px viewport, and the trajectory repeatedly notes horizontal overflow while interacting with the examples filter area.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal overflow makes touch exploration harder, hides content, and can obscure controls like the clear button or filter chips.
findings.suggestion: Rework the mobile layout to fit the viewport, stack controls vertically, and avoid fixed-width regions that force sideways scrolling.

findings.user_goal: Understand whether global search and keyboard navigation are working as intended
findings.problem: The command palette opens clearly, but keyboard interaction gives confusing navigation feedback because ArrowDown jumps away to a page anchor instead of visibly selecting a suggestion.
findings.evidence: On index.html and mobile index.html, Search docs ⌘K opened a centered overlay with input and hints, but ArrowDown led to api-reference.html#forge rather than an observable selection state in the palette.
findings.why_it_matters: Search is supposed to feel like a controlled, trustworthy shortcut. If arrow-key use unexpectedly moves the page, users may lose context and stop trusting the palette.
findings.suggestion: Keep keyboard focus inside the palette until Enter is pressed, show a visible highlighted suggestion, and only navigate after an explicit selection.

findings.user_goal: Use the version selector and other header controls with assistive tech
findings.problem: The version selector lacks an accessible name, which reduces discoverability and makes the control ambiguous for non-visual users.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly flag the header select as a missing_input_label on index.html, examples.html, and api-reference.html, and the element is described as unlabeled in the DOM summary.
findings.why_it_matters: An unlabeled select is difficult to announce or target with screen readers and can be especially confusing in a dense header with several similar controls.
findings.suggestion: Add a visible label or aria-label that explains what versions are being switched, and make the current version explicit.
findings.source_hint: Header select on index.html / examples.html / api-reference.html

findings.user_goal: Scan the examples gallery and choose the right filter quickly
findings.problem: Category chips on the examples page are visually compact, which weakens the filter bar’s prominence and makes the controls feel secondary to the content below.
findings.evidence: On mobile examples.html, the chips are only 27px tall and several are flagged as small tap targets; the same compact pattern appears on desktop with the filter row sitting close to the top of the card grid.
findings.why_it_matters: If filter controls are too small or visually quiet, users may miss the available narrowing options or struggle to switch categories confidently.
findings.suggestion: Increase chip height and spacing, and give the filter row a stronger container or section label so it reads as a primary control area.

findings.user_goal: Jump through the API reference efficiently
findings.problem: The page supports in-page anchors well, but the dense reference structure makes it easy to lose context in a long section list, especially on mobile where overflow is present.
findings.evidence: Clicks to asyncSlice() and derive() updated the hash and kept adjacent sections scannable, but the mobile API reference still shows horizontal overflow while deeper content remains in a dense table-like layout.
findings.why_it_matters: Even when anchors work, a crowded reference page can slow symbol lookup and make it harder to orient after a jump.
findings.suggestion: Add slightly stronger section separation and consider a sticky subsection index or jump bar for long reference pages on mobile.

findings.user_goal: Know whether placeholder top-nav destinations are real or intentionally unavailable
findings.problem: Some top navigation items appear as inert or placeholder links without clear feedback, which can make the site feel incomplete.
findings.evidence: The trajectory and unexplored features list show Blog and Community as clickable items, but prior actions reported no visible URL/text change for some top-bar probes and these destinations were not meaningfully exercised.
findings.why_it_matters: When a user sees a nav item that looks important but does nothing, they may question whether the docs are unfinished or broken.
findings.suggestion: If destinations are intentionally placeholders, label them clearly as coming soon; otherwise make the links visibly active and test their destination states.
